en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Maiden (Kumāribhūtavagga) 77.
The Training Rule on Not Ordaining a Trainee Nun (Sikkhamāna-navuṭṭhāpanasikkhāpada).
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain trainee nun approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and requested full ordination.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to that trainee nun,
"If you will give me a robe, noble lady, then I will ordain you," but she neither ordained her nor made any effort to have her ordained.
Then that trainee nun reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, disparaged it, and complained, saying:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā [admit] a trainee nun..."
‘If you, noble lady, will give me a robe, I will ordain you. Having said this, she neither ordains her nor makes any effort to have her ordained.

… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā, having said to a trainee nun, ‘If you, noble lady, will give me a robe, I will ordain you,’ neither ordains her nor makes any effort to have her ordained?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can this be, monks? How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā [act thus toward] a trainee nun?”
‘If you, noble lady, will give me a robe, I will ordain you. Having said this, she neither ordains her nor makes any effort toward her ordination.
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...

And so, monks, let the nuns recite this training rule: “Whatever nun, having made an appointment with a man, saying: ‘If you, noble sir, will give me a robe, I will ordain you,’ should neither ordain him nor make any effort toward his ordination, that nun is also to be dealt with according to the rule.”

“Whatever nun, having said to a trainee nun, ‘If you, noble lady, will give me a robe, I will ordain you,’ and afterwards, though there is no obstacle, neither ordains her nor makes an effort to have her ordained, commits an offense entailing confession. Regarding the phrase “whatever nun”:
[as defined previously].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... [as previously described] ... "a nun" ...
[as previously described] ... this is the nun intended in this context.
A *sikkhamānā* is one who has trained for two years in the six rules. "If you,
noble lady, will give me a robe, I shall ordain you."
In this way, I shall ordain her.
"She will subsequently have no obstacles" means that there will be no obstacle.
"Neither should she ordain her" means she should not ordain her herself.
"Nor should she make an effort toward her ordination" means...
One should not command another.

By the mere fact of relinquishing the burden with the thought, "I will neither give the full admission nor make an effort toward giving the full admission," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
If there is an obstacle,
or if she seeks it but does not obtain it,
or if she is ill.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
